messages:
maria: Heads up — after the v2.5.3 canary rollout we see a noticeable p95/p99 jump for the hotpath cohort (chat-heavy). p95 ~+120ms, p99 ~+420ms vs baseline. No increase in 5xxs. graphs: https://dash/reports/abc123 :eyes:
jon: thanks. which canary cohort/variant and what percentage rolled?
maria: canary variant=variant-b (new sidecar+telemetry shim), at 10% traffic. affected cohort = chat-heavy (longer context, many short requests).
alex: any auth or billing errors? or just latency?
maria: only latency. auth calls and embedding calls look normal. traces show increased tail in handler.span -> sidecar.sync flush -> epoll_wait. sample trace ids: t-42a1, t-42a4
jon: can you paste a short log snippet and a sample span timeline?
maria: ```
[2025-06-12T14:02:31Z] trace=t-42a1 handler.enter
[2025-06-12T14:02:31Z] trace=t-42a1 sidecar.sync start
[2025-06-12T14:02:31Z] trace=t-42a1 sidecar.sync wait epoll_wait +380ms
[2025-06-12T14:02:31Z] trace=t-42a1 handler.exit
```
tara: interesting — sidecar shim was recently changed to flush telemetry synchronously on request completion for better accuracy. hypothesis: sync flush adds blocking latency on hotpath.
jon: good call. can we reproduce locally with a small replay? run stressproxy against variant-b canary hosts with chat-heavy profile. command: `stressproxy replay --cohort chat-heavy --target canary-b --rps 200 --duration 5m`
maria: starting replay now, will attach flamegraph.
infra-bot: deploy/variant-b canary at 10% -> started (ci-98765) :rocket:
alex: while that's running, any kernel selector or scheduler changes in this runtime bump?
maria: runtime bump included kernel-selector tweak (more affinity to pack w/ quant processes) but that only affects long-running batches. the diff most likely is sidecar flush path.
tara: if replay reproduces, mitigation options: 1) quick toggle feature-flag to make sidecar async (buffer and background flush) 2) rollback sidecar image to previous tag on canary 3) shift canary traffic back to baseline variant (traffic-split 0/100). prefer 1 or 2 for faster rollback.
jon: I'll prepare a quick traffic-split experiment: route 50% of canary traffic to baseline variant and sample p95/p99. if p99 drops we isolate sidecar as primary suspect.
maria: traffic-split started -> canary split 50/50. watching p95 panel.
(2m later)
maria: p95 moved down ~80ms, p99 down ~350ms for the portion hitting baseline. portion still on variant-b retains the tail.
alex: confirms sidecar. what's the minimal fix? revert telemetry sync or revert the sidecar image to prev stable?
tara: revert telemetry change behind flag — faster. but sidecar image rollback safer if we want identical behavior. which is quicker for ops?
jon: ops can pin the sidecar image on canary hosts in minutes. I'll open a rollback patch and do a rolling restart of just canary hosts.
maria: opened rollback PR #4523 and started pin+restart on 4 canary hosts.
infra-bot: canary-host-12 restart -> success
infra-bot: canary-host-13 restart -> success
infra-bot: canary-host-14 restart -> success
infra-bot: canary-host-15 restart -> success
maria: after restart p95/p99 for canary dropped back to baseline. verified with traces: sidecar.sync no longer blocking.
support-bot: customer-alert: customer "AcmeCorp" reported increased latency earlier; sent update noting rollback and mitigation plan.
jon: plan for bisect / postmortem: 1) run controlled A/B at higher resolution across multiple cohorts 2) bisect the sidecar change that introduced sync flush 3) add e2e perf test in CI for hotpath cohort with sidecar enabled 4) follow-up: make telemetry flush async by default with backpressure cap and metric for dropped events.
ara: (typo — not in participants)
alex: small ops follow-ups: pin older sidecar image in dedicated hosts until patch validated; add alert for epoll wait tail >200ms in sidecar span.
tara: i'll write the rollback runbook steps and add to runbooks/playbooks. also add a short blameless note to eng-oncall.
maria: i'll escalate to SRE oncall if tail resurfaces in 30m. for now closing the immediate escalation — rollback successful. will follow-up with a short postmortem and action items. :white_check_mark: 
jon: thanks team. created the bisect ticket ENGRT-889 and assigned to tara/alex.
maria: summary for the record: root cause = sidecar telemetry sync flush on request completion added in sidecar v1.12. mitigation = rollback sidecar to v1.11 in canary + pin. next steps = async flush implementation + CI perf test + alerting. links: dashboard https://dash/reports/abc123, pr https://git/repo/pull/4523, ticket https://tracker/ENGRT-889
tara: nice work. :clap:
